content.user_title: Analyze Stocks with Graham and Buffett Frameworks
content.value_statement: Value investors need consistent analysis across valuation, quality, and financial statements. This skill applies structured Graham and Buffett frameworks with traceable data sources.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes one stock with Graham NCAV, valuation, dividend, debt, earnings stability, and value-trap checks.
Screens up to 300 securities using Graham filters and ranks qualified deep-value candidates.
Evaluates economic moats, financial health, management, valuation, and long-term visibility for one stock.
Screens Buffett-style quality compounders using quantitative gates followed by qualitative moat scoring.
Reconciles income, balance-sheet, and cash-flow figures before issuing scores.
Documents Longbridge and WebSearch sources in a data appendix.
limitations: Primary analysis requires available Longbridge CLI or MCP market data.
WebSearch is limited to genuine gaps and may not provide complete qualitative evidence.
Referenced scoring, criteria, and output template files are absent from this package.
Results are informational and do not replace professional financial advice.

use_cases.title: Review a Deep-Value Stock
use_cases.description: Assess one ticker against Graham criteria, liquidation value, safety margin, and value-trap indicators.

use_cases.title: Research Business Quality
use_cases.description: Evaluate a company moat, financial durability, management record, valuation, and expected holding period.

use_cases.title: Build a Candidate List
use_cases.description: Screen an index or watchlist for Graham bargains or Buffett-style quality compounders.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Graham Candidate
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze {ticker} with the Graham framework. Show NCAV, valuation filters, safety margin, holding period, value-trap warnings, and sources.

prompt_templates.title: Assess One Buffett Candidate
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze {ticker} using the Buffett moat framework. Rate each dimension, separate business quality from price, and cite every material figure.

prompt_templates.title: Screen a Market Universe
prompt_templates.prompt: Screen {index_or_watchlist} in {market} for {Graham_or_Buffett} candidates. Use default thresholds, explain exclusions, and return ranked results with sources.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Frameworks with Sensitivity
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconcile statements for {ticker}, then compare Graham and Buffett conclusions. Test {threshold_changes}, identify conflicting signals, and explain data limitations.

output_examples.output: A structured report covers NCAV, valuation, debt coverage, earnings stability, dynamic warnings, holding period, safety margin, and cited data sources.

output_examples.input: Would Buffett consider AAPL.US under this framework?
output_examples.output: A five-dimension moat assessment separates business quality from valuation and closes with evidence, holding-period expectations, limitations, and a disclaimer.

output_examples.input: Screen my 40-stock watchlist for quality compounders.
output_examples.output: A short candidate set shows filter results, moat evidence, valuation tiers, exclusions, reconciliation status, and a source appendix.

best_practices: Provide a market-qualified ticker or a clearly defined index or watchlist.
State any threshold changes before screening so results remain comparable.
Review the source appendix and data limitations before using any score.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a high score as a direct buy or sell recommendation.
Do not compare NCAV across banks, insurers, REITs, or other excluded financial structures.
Do not use stale or unreconciled financial statements when current data is available.

faq.question: Which investing frameworks are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports Graham NCAV and defensive filters plus Buffett moat and quality-compounder analysis.

faq.question: Can it analyze one stock?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides separate Graham and Buffett single-stock workflows.

faq.question: Can it screen an index or watchlist?
faq.answer: Yes. Graham screening supports up to 300 names, while Buffett screening returns three to five candidates.

faq.question: Where does the financial data come from?
faq.answer: It uses Longbridge CLI first, MCP as a fallback, and WebSearch only for genuine data gaps.

faq.question: Does it verify financial statement consistency?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks cross-statement relationships and halts or excludes results when differences exceed stated tolerances.

faq.question: Does this skill provide investment advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured research for informational use and includes explicit investment disclaimers.
